purpose: Hyoscyamine is used to relieve stomach and intestinal cramps, spasms, and pain. It can also help with conditions like irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), bladder problems, and peptic ulcers. Doctors sometimes use it to reduce excess saliva or secretions before surgery.
how_it_works: Your body uses a chemical called acetylcholine to send signals that cause muscles to squeeze and contract. Hyoscyamine blocks those signals, which helps the muscles in your stomach, intestines, and bladder relax. Think of it like pressing a pause button on the cramping and spasms so you feel more comfortable.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth is the most common side effect. You may also notice blurry vision, difficulty urinating, constipation, a faster heartbeat, dizziness, drowsiness, flushing, or decreased sweating. Most of these happen because the medicine is relaxing smooth muscles and reducing secretions throughout your body.
warnings: Be very careful in hot weather because this medicine reduces your ability to sweat, which can cause overheating or heatstroke. Do not drive or use heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause drowsiness or blurry vision. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, urinary problems, or heart disease, as this medication may not be safe for you. Avoid alcohol while taking it. Keep out of reach of children — accidental overdose is dangerous.
typical_dosing: For adults and children over 12, the usual dose is 0.125 mg to 0.25 mg taken by mouth every 4 hours as needed, but no more than 1.5 mg in a 24-hour period. Extended-release tablets are usually taken every 8 to 12 hours. Always follow exactly what your doctor or pharmacist tells you, since dosing can vary based on your condition and age.
